pages.text: Weigh a helium nucleus and it is lighter than its two protons and two neutrons were apart, by about 0.03 atomic mass units. That missing mass is the $(thing)binding energy$(): B = Δm·c², 28.3 MeV for helium-4 - several million times what a chemical bond holds.

Binding energy per nucleon rises from hydrogen to iron and falls after it. Split a heavy nucleus or fuse two light ones, and both ways climb towards iron and release energy. Fission and fusion are where this leads.
